children: *Five-Year U.S. Treasury Clears at 5.033%, Highest Auction Yield Since June 2006
U.S. Treasury Pays Highest Five-Year Yield in Auction in Two Decades
The U.S. Treasury auctioned $70 billion in five-year notes and investors demanded a steep return.
The notes sold on Wednesday at a yield of 5.033%, the highest since an auction held in June 2006, which had a high yield of 5.203%.
Demand indicators were soft. The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.21, lower than the previous six-month average of 2.33.
The auction's yield was substantially higher than the 5.002% when-issued yield at the time of the tender. The tail, in bond markets parlance, was another sign of weak demand.
Following the auction results, the on-the-run five-year yield traded at 5.023%, according to Tradeweb.
